title: Ratios and Rates
seo_title: Grade 6 Ratios and Rates Worksheets: Unit Rates and Better Buys (TEKS 6.4, STAAR)
standard_text: 6.4B apply qualitative and quantitative reasoning to solve prediction and comparison of real-world problems involving ratios and rates; 6.4C give examples of ratios as multiplicative comparisons of two quantities describing the same attribute; 6.4D give examples of rates as the comparison by division of two quantities having different attributes, including rates as quotients
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 ratio and rate worksheets for Texas TEKS 6.4B, 6.4C and 6.4D: write ratios, ratio language, equivalent ratios, unit rates and better buys. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A ratio compares two quantities; a unit rate is the amount for 1.
key_sub: 3 : 5 is not the same as 5 : 3. $4.50 for 3 is $1.50 each.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A ratio compares two quantities by multiplication: 3 cats for every 5 dogs is 3 : 5.
  • The order matters: dogs to cats is 5 : 3.
  • A rate compares quantities with different units, such as 120 miles in 2 hours.
  • A unit rate is the amount for 1: 120 ÷ 2 = 60 miles per hour.

Examples

Example

$4.50 for 3 muffins

$4.50 ÷ 3

Answer: $1.50 per muffin

Example

Which is simpler, 12 : 18 or 2 : 3?

12 ÷ 6 = 2, 18 ÷ 6 = 3

Answer: 2 : 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing the ratio in the wrong orderFollow the order of the words: trucks to cars.
Mixing up part-to-part and part-to-wholePart-to-whole uses the total.
Dividing the wrong way for a unit rateDivide by the quantity you want 1 of.

faq.a: Give examples of ratios as multiplicative comparisons of two quantities describing the same attribute.
Give examples of rates as the comparison by division of two quantities having different attributes, including rates as quotients.

faq.q: What is the difference between a ratio and a rate?
faq.a: A rate compares quantities with different units, like miles and hours.

faq.q: How do I find the better buy?
faq.a: Find the unit price of each and choose the lower one.

sets.title: Write a ratio from a picture

items.q: What is the ratio of triangles to circles?
items.e: Count only the two kinds named: 3 triangles and 6 circles. Triangles come first, so the ratio is 3:6. Leave out the squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 6 squares and 4 circles. Squares are named first, so write 6 first: 6:4. 4:6 would compare circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to all the shapes?
items.e: There are 4 circles and 4 + 3 = 7 shapes in all. Circles to all shapes is 4:7. 4:3 compares circles to squares, not to all the shapes.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 8 squares and 3 circles. Squares are named first, so write 8 first: 8:3. 3:8 would compare circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to triangles?
items.e: Count only the two kinds named: 4 circles and 6 triangles. Circles come first, so the ratio is 4:6. Leave out the squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 4 circles and 5 squares. Circles are named first, so write 4 first: 4:5. 5:4 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: Which sentence describes the picture?
c: For every 6 circles, there are 5 squares.
For every 5 circles, there are 6 squares.
For every 5 shapes, there are 6 squares.
For every 5 circles, there are 11 squares.
items.e: There are 5 circles and 6 squares, so the ratio of circles to squares is 5:6: for every 5 circles, there are 6 squares. There are 11 shapes in all, not 5.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to triangles?
items.e: Count only the two kinds named: 5 squares and 6 triangles. Squares come first, so the ratio is 5:6. Leave out the circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 7 circles and 2 squares. Circles are named first, so write 7 first: 7:2. 2:7 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: Which sentence describes the picture?
c: For every 2 circles, there are 4 squares.
For every 2 circles, there are 6 squares.
For every 2 shapes, there are 4 squares.
For every 4 circles, there are 2 squares.
items.e: There are 2 circles and 4 squares, so the ratio of circles to squares is 2:4: for every 2 circles, there are 4 squares. There are 6 shapes in all, not 2.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to all the shapes?
items.e: There are 7 squares and 5 + 7 = 12 shapes in all. Squares to all shapes is 7:12. 7:5 compares squares to circles, not to all the shapes.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to all the shapes?
items.e: There are 3 squares and 8 + 3 = 11 shapes in all. Squares to all shapes is 3:11. 3:8 compares squares to circles, not to all the shapes.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 6 squares and 8 circles. Squares are named first, so write 6 first: 6:8. 8:6 would compare circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 3 squares and 2 circles. Squares are named first, so write 3 first: 3:2. 2:3 would compare circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to all the shapes?
items.e: There are 8 circles and 8 + 2 = 10 shapes in all. Circles to all shapes is 8:10. 8:2 compares circles to squares, not to all the shapes.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 5 circles and 8 squares. Circles are named first, so write 5 first: 5:8. 8:5 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 7 circles and 4 squares. Circles are named first, so write 7 first: 7:4. 4:7 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 4 circles and 8 squares. Circles are named first, so write 4 first: 4:8. 8:4 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 6 circles and 7 squares. Circles are named first, so write 6 first: 6:7. 7:6 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: Which sentence describes the picture?
c: For every 3 circles, there are 7 squares.
For every 7 circles, there are 10 squares.
For every 7 circles, there are 3 squares.
For every 7 shapes, there are 3 squares.
items.e: There are 7 circles and 3 squares, so the ratio of circles to squares is 7:3: for every 7 circles, there are 3 squares. There are 10 shapes in all, not 7.

items.q: A parking lot has 11 cars and 4 trucks. What is the ratio of trucks to all the vehicles?
items.e: All the vehicles: 11 + 4 = 15. Trucks to all the vehicles is 4:15. This is a part-to-whole ratio.

items.q: A fish tank has only goldfish and guppies. The ratio of goldfish to guppies is 5:6. What is the ratio of guppies to all the fish?
items.e: For every 5 goldfish there are 6 guppies, so every group has 5 + 6 = 11 fish. Guppies to all is 6:11.

items.q: A class has 21 students. 5 of them are girls, and the rest are boys. What is the ratio of boys to girls?
items.e: Boys: 21 − 5 = 16. Boys to girls is 16:5. Use the two parts, not the total, 21.

items.q: A fish tank has only goldfish and guppies. The ratio of goldfish to guppies is 3:2. Which sentence means the same thing?
c: For every 2 fish, there are 3 goldfish.
For every 3 goldfish, there are 5 guppies.
For every 3 goldfish, there are 2 guppies.
For every 3 guppies, there are 2 goldfish.
items.e: 3:2 means for every 3 goldfish, there are 2 guppies. The first number goes with goldfish, the second with guppies.

items.q: A running club has 9 sixth graders and 13 fifth graders. What is the ratio of sixth graders to all the runners?
items.e: All the runners: 9 + 13 = 22. Sixth graders to all the runners is 9:22. This is a part-to-whole ratio.

items.q: A school band has 15 drummers and 4 trumpet players. What is the ratio of trumpet players to all the band members?
items.e: All the band members: 15 + 4 = 19. Trumpet players to all the band members is 4:19. This is a part-to-whole ratio.

items.q: A running club has only sixth graders and fifth graders. The ratio of sixth graders to fifth graders is 7:4. What fraction of the runners are sixth graders?
items.e: Out of every 7 + 4 = 11 runners, 7 are sixth graders. So 711 of the runners are sixth graders, not 74.

items.q: A garden has only tulips and daisies. The ratio of tulips to daisies is 5:3. What is the ratio of daisies to all the flowers?
items.e: For every 5 tulips there are 3 daisies, so every group has 5 + 3 = 8 flowers. Daisies to all is 3:8.

items.q: A bag has 29 marbles. 15 of them are red marbles, and the rest are blue marbles. What is the ratio of blue marbles to red marbles?
items.e: Blue marbles: 29 − 15 = 14. Blue marbles to red marbles is 14:15. Use the two parts, not the total, 29.

items.q: A bookshelf has only novels and comic books. The ratio of novels to comic books is 5:4. What fraction of the books are novels?
items.e: Out of every 5 + 4 = 9 books, 5 are novels. So 59 of the books are novels, not 54.

items.q: On a bookshelf, for every 6 novels, there are 5 comic books. What is the ratio of comic books to novels?
items.e: The question asks for comic books first, then novels. There are 5 comic books for every 6 novels, so the ratio is 5:6.

items.q: An animal shelter has only cats and dogs. The ratio of cats to dogs is 6:1. Which sentence means the same thing?
c: For every 6 dogs, there is 1 cat.
For every animal, there are 6 cats.
For every 6 cats, there is 1 dog.
For every 6 cats, there are 7 dogs.
items.e: 6:1 means for every 6 cats, there is 1 dog. The first number goes with cats, the second with dogs.

items.q: A farm has only cows and horses. The ratio of cows to horses is 2:5. Which also shows this ratio?
items.e: 2:5 and “2 to 5” mean the same thing. Keep the order: cows first, then horses.

items.q: A garden has only tulips and daisies. The ratio of tulips to daisies is 3:5. Which also shows this ratio?
items.e: 3:5 and “3 to 5” mean the same thing. Keep the order: tulips first, then daisies.

items.q: A class has only girls and boys. The ratio of girls to boys is 2:7. Which also shows this ratio?
items.e: 2:7 and “2 to 7” mean the same thing. Keep the order: girls first, then boys.

items.q: A farm has 20 animals. 12 of them are cows, and the rest are horses. What is the ratio of horses to cows?
items.e: Horses: 20 − 12 = 8. Horses to cows is 8:12. Use the two parts, not the total, 20.

items.q: A fruit bowl has 6 apples and 9 oranges. What is the ratio of apples to all the pieces of fruit?
items.e: All the pieces of fruit: 6 + 9 = 15. Apples to all the pieces of fruit is 6:15. This is a part-to-whole ratio.

items.q: A basket has only red peppers and green peppers. The ratio of red peppers to green peppers is 5:2. What fraction of the peppers are red peppers?
items.e: Out of every 5 + 2 = 7 peppers, 5 are red peppers. So 57 of the peppers are red peppers, not 52.

items.q: In a basket, for every 3 red peppers, there are 7 green peppers. What is the ratio of green peppers to red peppers?
items.e: The question asks for green peppers first, then red peppers. There are 7 green peppers for every 3 red peppers, so the ratio is 7:3.

items.q: An animal shelter has only cats and dogs. The ratio of cats to dogs is 4:5. What is the ratio of dogs to all the animals?
items.e: For every 4 cats there are 5 dogs, so every group has 4 + 5 = 9 animals. Dogs to all is 5:9.

items.q: 8:5 = ☐:25. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 5 × 5 = 25, so multiply the first term by 5 too: 8 × 5 = 40. Adding 20 to both terms would give 28, which is wrong.

items.q: 9:5 = 54:☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 9 × 6 = 54, so multiply the second term by 6 too: 5 × 6 = 30. Adding 45 to both terms would give 50, which is wrong.

items.q: 5:7 = 20:☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 5 × 4 = 20, so multiply the second term by 4 too: 7 × 4 = 28. Adding 15 to both terms would give 22, which is wrong.

items.q: Which ratio is not equivalent to 9:6?
items.e: 9:6 simplifies to 3:2. 36:24 and 27:18 are 9:6 with both terms multiplied by the same number. 10:7 adds 1 to both terms, so it is not equivalent.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 7:5?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 3: 7 × 3 = 21 and 5 × 3 = 15. Adding 3 to both terms (10:8) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 1:2?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 3: 1 × 3 = 3 and 2 × 3 = 6. Adding 3 to both terms (4:5) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: What is 64:24 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 8, the greatest number that divides both: 64 ÷ 8 = 8 and 24 ÷ 8 = 3. So 64:24 = 8:3. Subtracting 8 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: What is 21:56 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 7, the greatest number that divides both: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 and 56 ÷ 7 = 8. So 21:56 = 3:8. Subtracting 7 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which two ratios are equivalent to each other?
items.e: 10:6 and 20:12 both simplify to 5:3. Adding the same number to both terms, or switching the order, makes a different ratio.

items.q: 4:9 = ☐:72. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 9 × 8 = 72, so multiply the first term by 8 too: 4 × 8 = 32. Adding 63 to both terms would give 67, which is wrong.

items.q: What is 8:6 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 2, the greatest number that divides both: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 and 6 ÷ 2 = 3. So 8:6 = 4:3. Subtracting 2 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 9:1?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 5: 9 × 5 = 45 and 1 × 5 = 5. Adding 5 to both terms (14:6) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which pair of ratios is equivalent?
items.e: 6:8 and 12:16 both simplify to 3:4. Adding the same number to both terms, or switching the order, makes a different ratio.

items.q: What is 45:10 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 5, the greatest number that divides both: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 and 10 ÷ 5 = 2. So 45:10 = 9:2. Subtracting 5 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 5:6?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 6: 5 × 6 = 30 and 6 × 6 = 36. Adding 6 to both terms (11:12) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: What is 10:18 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 2, the greatest number that divides both: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 18 ÷ 2 = 9. So 10:18 = 5:9. Subtracting 2 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 9:4?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 2: 9 × 2 = 18 and 4 × 2 = 8. Adding 2 to both terms (11:6) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: 5:9 = ☐:27. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 9 × 3 = 27, so multiply the first term by 3 too: 5 × 3 = 15. Adding 18 to both terms would give 23, which is wrong.

items.q: Each tricycle has 3 wheels and 1 seat. A store has 5 tricycles. What is the ratio of seats to wheels in simplest form?
items.e: 5 tricycles have 5 seats and 5 × 3 = 15 wheels. Seats to wheels is 5:15 = 1:3: for every 1 seat, there are 3 wheels.

items.q: What is 10:16 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 2, the greatest number that divides both: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 16 ÷ 2 = 8. So 10:16 = 5:8. Subtracting 2 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: A car drives 120 miles in 2 hours at a steady speed. How many miles per hour is that?
c: 160 mile per hour
items.e: “Per hour” means for 1 hour. Divide: 120 miles ÷ 2 hours = 60 miles per hour. Check: 60 × 2 = 120. “60 hours per mile” has the units backwards. 2 ÷ 120 divides the wrong way. 120 × 2 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A printer prints 150 pages in 5 minutes. How many pages per minute does it print?
c: 130 page per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 150 pages ÷ 5 minutes = 30 pages per minute. Check: 30 × 5 = 150. 5 ÷ 150 divides the wrong way. 150 × 5 multiplies instead of dividing. “30 minutes per page” has the units backwards.

items.q: Valeria types 180 words in 4 minutes. How many words per minute does she type?
c: 145 word per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 180 words ÷ 4 minutes = 45 words per minute. Check: 45 × 4 = 180. 180 × 4 multiplies instead of dividing. “45 minutes per word” has the units backwards. 4 ÷ 180 divides the wrong way.

items.q: Marcus reads 96 pages in 3 days. How many pages does he read per day?
c: 132 page per day
items.e: “Per day” means for 1 day. Divide: 96 pages ÷ 3 days = 32 pages per day. Check: 32 × 3 = 96. “32 days per page” has the units backwards. 96 × 3 multiplies instead of dividing. 3 ÷ 96 divides the wrong way.

items.q: Sofia walks 12 miles in 4 hours. What is her walking speed?
c: 13 mile per hour
items.e: “Per hour” means for 1 hour. Divide: 12 miles ÷ 4 hours = 3 miles per hour. Check: 3 × 4 = 12. 4 ÷ 12 divides the wrong way. “3 hours per mile” has the units backwards. 12 × 4 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A train travels 260 miles in 4 hours. What is its speed in miles per hour?
c: 165 mile per hour
items.e: “Per hour” means for 1 hour. Divide: 260 miles ÷ 4 hours = 65 miles per hour. Check: 65 × 4 = 260. 260 × 4 multiplies instead of dividing. 4 ÷ 260 divides the wrong way. “65 hours per mile” has the units backwards.

items.q: Carlos rides a bike 36 miles in 3 hours. How many miles per hour does he ride?
c: 112 mile per hour
items.e: “Per hour” means for 1 hour. Divide: 36 miles ÷ 3 hours = 12 miles per hour. Check: 12 × 3 = 36. “12 hours per mile” has the units backwards. 3 ÷ 36 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A garden hose fills a 45-gallon tub in 9 minutes. How many gallons per minute flow from the hose?
c: 15 gallon per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 45 gallons ÷ 9 minutes = 5 gallons per minute. Check: 5 × 9 = 45. 9 ÷ 45 divides the wrong way. “5 minutes per gallon” has the units backwards.

items.q: Elijah counts that his heart beats 225 times in 3 minutes. What is his heart rate?
c: 175 beat per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 225 beats ÷ 3 minutes = 75 beats per minute. Check: 75 × 3 = 225. “75 minutes per beat” has the units backwards. 225 × 3 multiplies instead of dividing. 3 ÷ 225 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A car uses 4 gallons of gas to drive 112 miles. How many miles per gallon does it get?
c: 128 mile per gallon
items.e: “Per gallon” means for 1 gallon. Divide: 112 miles ÷ 4 gallons = 28 miles per gallon. Check: 28 × 4 = 112. “28 gallons per mile” has the units backwards. 4 ÷ 112 divides the wrong way. 112 × 4 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A baker uses 24 eggs for 8 cakes. How many eggs does the baker use for each cake?
c: 13 egg for each cake
items.e: “For each cake” means for 1 cake. Divide: 24 eggs ÷ 8 cakes = 3 eggs for each cake. Check: 3 × 8 = 24. “3 cakes for each egg” has the units backwards. 8 ÷ 24 divides the wrong way.

items.q: A school gives out 168 pencils to 24 students. Each student gets the same number. How many pencils is that for each student?
c: 17 pencil for each student
items.e: “For each student” means for 1 student. Divide: 168 pencils ÷ 24 students = 7 pencils for each student. Check: 7 × 24 = 168. 24 ÷ 168 divides the wrong way. “7 students for each pencil” has the units backwards.

items.q: 84 students ride 3 buses to a field trip. Each bus has the same number of students. How many students are there per bus?
items.e: “Per bus” means for 1 bus. Divide: 84 students ÷ 3 buses = 28 students per bus. Check: 28 × 3 = 84. 84 × 3 multiplies instead of dividing. “28 buses per student” has the units backwards.

items.q: Grace swims 20 laps in 10 minutes. How many laps per minute does she swim?
c: 12 lap per minute
items.e: “Per minute” means for 1 minute. Divide: 20 laps ÷ 10 minutes = 2 laps per minute. Check: 2 × 10 = 20. 10 ÷ 20 divides the wrong way. “2 minutes per lap” has the units backwards. 20 × 10 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: A bean plant grows 14 inches in 7 weeks. How many inches per week does it grow?
c: 12 inch per week
items.e: “Per week” means for 1 week. Divide: 14 inches ÷ 7 weeks = 2 inches per week. Check: 2 × 7 = 14. 14 × 7 multiplies instead of dividing. 7 ÷ 14 divides the wrong way. “2 weeks per inch” has the units backwards.

items.q: A cheetah runs 300 meters in 10 seconds. How many meters per second is that?
c: 130 meter per second
items.e: “Per second” means for 1 second. Divide: 300 meters ÷ 10 seconds = 30 meters per second. Check: 30 × 10 = 300. “30 seconds per meter” has the units backwards. 10 ÷ 300 divides the wrong way. 300 × 10 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Which rate is a unit rate?
items.e: A unit rate tells how much for 1 unit. “55 miles per hour” means 55 miles in 1 hour. The others compare to 2, 3 or 4 units.

items.q: What does “per” mean in “28 miles per gallon”?
items.e: “Per” means for each (or for 1). The car goes 28 miles for each gallon of gas.

items.q: A car drives 150 miles in 3 hours. Which problem finds the miles per hour?
items.e: Miles per hour = miles ÷ hours. Put the miles first: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 miles per hour. 3 ÷ 150 would give hours per mile.

items.q: Mateo runs 9 laps in 3 minutes. He says his rate is 13 lap per minute. What is the correct rate?
items.e: Mateo divided the wrong way (3 ÷ 9). Laps per minute = laps ÷ minutes: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 laps per minute. Check: 3 × 3 = 9 laps.

sets.title: Compare rates: the better buy and the faster speed

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Box A: 12 ounces of cereal for $3.00
Box B: 20 ounces of cereal for $4.00
c: Both cost the same per ounce
items.e: Compare the price for 1 ounce, not the total price. Box A: $3.00 ÷ 12 = $0.25 per ounce. Box B: $4.00 ÷ 20 = $0.20 per ounce. Box B costs less per ounce, so it is the better buy. (Box A costs less in total, but you get less.)

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Bottle A: 64 ounces of juice for $3.84
Bottle B: 32 ounces of juice for $2.24
c: Both cost the same per ounce
items.e: Compare the price for 1 ounce, not the total price. Bottle A: $3.84 ÷ 64 = $0.06 per ounce. Bottle B: $2.24 ÷ 32 = $0.07 per ounce. Bottle A costs less per ounce, so it is the better buy. (Bottle B costs less in total, but you get less.)

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Bag A: 1 pound of pasta for $1.50
Bag B: 3 pounds of pasta for $4.20
c: Both cost the same per pound
items.e: Compare the price for 1 pound, not the total price. Bag A: $1.50 ÷ 1 = $1.50 per pound. Bag B: $4.20 ÷ 3 = $1.40 per pound. Bag B costs less per pound, so it is the better buy. (Bag A costs less in total, but you get less.)

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Pack A: 10 pencils for $2.50
Pack B: 24 pencils for $5.28
c: Both cost the same per pencil
items.e: Compare the price for 1 pencil, not the total price. Pack A: $2.50 ÷ 10 = $0.25 per pencil. Pack B: $5.28 ÷ 24 = $0.22 per pencil. Pack B costs less per pencil, so it is the better buy. (Pack A costs less in total, but you get less.)

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Carton A: 12 eggs for $3.60
Carton B: 18 eggs for $5.40
c: Both cost the same per egg
items.e: Compare the price for 1 egg, not the total price. Carton A: $3.60 ÷ 12 = $0.30 per egg. Carton B: $5.40 ÷ 18 = $0.30 per egg. The unit prices are equal, so neither is a better buy.

items.q:
Which is the better buy?
Pack A: 4 cups of yogurt for $2.00
Pack B: 6 cups of yogurt for $3.30
c: Both cost the same per cup
items.e: Compare the price for 1 cup, not the total price. Pack A: $2.00 ÷ 4 = $0.50 per cup. Pack B: $3.30 ÷ 6 = $0.55 per cup. Pack A costs less per cup, so it is the better buy.

items.q:
Which bag of rice costs the least per pound?
2-pound bag: $3.00
5-pound bag: $6.50
10-pound bag: $12.00
c: They all cost the same per pound
items.e: Find each price per pound: 2-pound bag: $3.00 ÷ 2 = $1.50 per pound; 5-pound bag: $6.50 ÷ 5 = $1.30 per pound; 10-pound bag: $12.00 ÷ 10 = $1.20 per pound. The lowest unit price is $1.20 per pound, so the 10-pound bag is the best buy.

items.q:
Which bag of apples costs the least per pound?
3-pound bag: $4.35
5-pound bag: $6.95
8-pound bag: $11.60
c: They all cost the same per pound
items.e: Find each price per pound: 3-pound bag: $4.35 ÷ 3 = $1.45 per pound; 5-pound bag: $6.95 ÷ 5 = $1.39 per pound; 8-pound bag: $11.60 ÷ 8 = $1.45 per pound. The lowest unit price is $1.39 per pound, so the 5-pound bag is the best buy.

items.q:
Which pack of water costs the least per bottle?
6-pack: $3.00
12-pack: $5.40
24-pack: $11.04
c: They all cost the same per bottle
items.e: Find each price per bottle: 6-pack: $3.00 ÷ 6 = $0.50 per bottle; 12-pack: $5.40 ÷ 12 = $0.45 per bottle; 24-pack: $11.04 ÷ 24 = $0.46 per bottle. The lowest unit price is $0.45 per bottle, so the 12-pack is the best buy.

items.q: Grace walks 6 miles in 2 hours. Josiah walks 10 miles in 4 hours. Who walks faster?
c: Both walk at the same rate
Cannot tell, the times are different
items.e: Find each unit rate. Grace: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 miles per hour. Josiah: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 miles per hour. Grace has the greater unit rate. (Josiah walks farther in total, but takes more time.)

items.q: Car A goes 165 miles in 3 hours. Car B goes 240 miles in 4 hours. Which car is faster?
c: Cannot tell, the times are different
Both drive at the same rate
items.e: Find each unit rate. Car A: 165 ÷ 3 = 55 miles per hour. Car B: 240 ÷ 4 = 60 miles per hour. Car B has the greater unit rate.

items.q: Ethan types 150 words in 3 minutes. Noah types 245 words in 5 minutes. Who types faster?
c: Both type at the same rate
Cannot tell, the times are different
items.e: Find each unit rate. Ethan: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 words per minute. Noah: 245 ÷ 5 = 49 words per minute. Ethan has the greater unit rate. (Noah types more words in total, but takes more time.)

items.q: Valeria runs 3 miles in 30 minutes. Emma runs 5 miles in 50 minutes. Who runs faster?
c: Cannot tell, the times are different
Both run at the same rate
items.e: Find each unit rate. Valeria: 3 ÷ 30 = 0.1 mile per minute. Emma: 5 ÷ 50 = 0.1 mile per minute. The unit rates are equal, so they run at the same rate.

items.q: Faucet A fills 12 gallons in 4 minutes. Faucet B fills 25 gallons in 10 minutes. Which faucet fills faster?
c: Cannot tell, the times are different
Both fill at the same rate
items.e: Find each unit rate. Faucet A: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 gallons per minute. Faucet B: 25 ÷ 10 = 2.5 gallons per minute. Faucet A has the greater unit rate. (Faucet B fills more water in total, but takes more time.)

items.q: Recipe A uses 2 cups of sugar for 3 cups of flour. Recipe B uses 3 cups of sugar for 4 cups of flour. Which recipe uses more sugar for each cup of flour?
items.e: Sugar per cup of flour: A: 2 ÷ 3 = 23 cup. B: 3 ÷ 4 = 34 cup. 23 = 812 and 34 = 912, so Recipe B uses more sugar per cup of flour.

items.q: Car A drives 336 miles on 12 gallons of gas. Car B drives 300 miles on 10 gallons. Which car goes farther on 1 gallon?
items.e: Miles per gallon: A: 336 ÷ 12 = 28. B: 300 ÷ 10 = 30. Car B goes farther on each gallon. (Car A goes more miles in total, but it uses more gas.)

items.q: Ava earns $45 for 4 hours of work. Marcus earns $56 for 5 hours. Who earns more per hour?
c: They earn the same per hour
items.e: Ava: $45 ÷ 4 = $11.25 per hour. Marcus: $56 ÷ 5 = $11.20 per hour. Ava earns $0.05 more per hour, even though Marcus earns more in total.

items.q: An 18-ounce jar of peanut butter costs $3.60. A 12-ounce jar costs $2.76. How much less per ounce does the better buy cost?
items.e: 18-ounce jar: $3.60 ÷ 18 = $0.20 per ounce. 12-ounce jar: $2.76 ÷ 12 = $0.23 per ounce. $0.23 − $0.20 = $0.03 less per ounce. ($0.84 is the difference of the total prices.)

items.q: Store A sells 4 pounds of bananas for $2.36. Store B sells 3 pounds for $1.86. What is the lower price per pound?
items.e: Store A: $2.36 ÷ 4 = $0.59 per pound. Store B: $1.86 ÷ 3 = $0.62 per pound. The lower price per pound is $0.59, at Store A.

items.q: A 2-pound bag of rice costs $3.00 and a 5-pound bag costs $6.50. Isabella says the 2-pound bag is the better buy because $3.00 is less than $6.50. What should she compare?
items.e: Compare the price per pound. 2-pound bag: $3.00 ÷ 2 = $1.50 per pound. 5-pound bag: $6.50 ÷ 5 = $1.30 per pound. The 5-pound bag is the better buy.
